concepts.title: Measures of Central Tendency
concepts.definition: A measure of central tendency summarises a data series by one typical value: the arithmetic mean divides the sum of values by their number, the median is the middle value of the ordered series, and the mode is the most frequently occurring value.
concepts.key_idea: The arithmetic mean equals the sum of all values divided by how many values there are.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy302.txt mean, median and mode definitions and computation

solution_steps.explain: the numerator of the mean is the sum of the series
the mean is sum over count

concepts.title: Computing the Median
concepts.definition: The median is found by arranging values in ascending order and taking the middle value; for an even number of observations the median is the average of the two middle values, making it resistant to extremes.
concepts.key_idea: With an even number of ordered values the median is the average of the two central values.

solution_steps.explain: order the series and pick the central pair

concepts.title: Measures of Dispersion
concepts.definition: Dispersion measures how values spread around the central value; the range is the difference between the largest and smallest values, the mean deviation averages absolute distances from the mean, and the standard deviation squares distances before averaging, giving the most used spread measure.
concepts.key_idea: The range of a data series is the largest value minus the smallest value.

solution_steps.explain: the largest and smallest values bound the spread

concepts.title: Processing Steps for Geographic Data
concepts.definition: Data processing runs from editing and coding collected figures, classifying them into class intervals, tallying frequencies and computing summary measures, so that raw field sheets become analysable frequency tables ready for graphs and maps.
concepts.key_idea: Classification into class intervals is the bridge between raw numbers and every table, graph and map that follows.
